advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make check_workflows assert it matched at least one astral-sh/setup-uv call site (fail if zero), so an empty override scan cannot masquerade as 'all sites clean'.
evidence: scripts/check_uv_pin.py:148 docstring: 'Assert no ``setup-uv`` call site overrides the single source with its own input.'

scripts/check_uv_pin.py:154-171 iterates workflows and only appends a Finding when an OVERRIDING_INPUTS key is present; there is no counter of matched setup-uv steps and no failure when zero steps match SETUP_UV_ACTION

Litmus: the world 'the SETUP_UV_ACTION substring matched nothing (renamed/moved action)' yields the same empty result as 'all sites clean', so the pass verdict is indistinguishable from the check not having run against any site.
advisory.finding: check_workflows flags per-call-site version:/version-file: overrides but never asserts it actually matched any astral-sh/setup-uv step. If the action is renamed, moved into a composite action outside .github/workflows, or SETUP_UV_ACTION drifts, the scan produces zero findings — identical output to having inspected all 25 clean sites. The check cannot distinguish 'checked and clean' from 'matched nothing'.
scenarios: A future refactor pins setup-uv under a different owner/name or wraps it in .github/actions/*; the gate goes green while a per-site override could re-introduce the divergence the ticket's third AC targets.
The action's step comment/format changes such that the uses value no longer startswith the exact match string.
advisory.suggested_fix: Count matched setup-uv steps across all workflows and emit a Finding when the count is 0 (e.g. 'expected >=1 setup-uv call site to govern, found none — has the action been renamed or moved?'), before returning the (possibly empty) override findings.
